clue.text: Lets gran adjust throttle

indicators.note: to adjust something is to rearrange it, so the preceding words are put into a new order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to let grandmother fiddle with an engine's throttle.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle someone is to choke them by the neck, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Aggravation the two of them brought to the queen?

parts.note: a word meaning the pair together
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A pair of troublemakers hauled before the monarch for causing aggravation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother as a noun means trouble or annoyance, the same sense as aggravation in informal speech.

clue.text: Ineffectual type made off with outside chance

indicators.note: the second word is placed around the outside of the first, enclosing it
something off has gone wrong, so the word before it is scrambled

parts.note: the word rearranged
chance or fortune

explanation.surface: Someone useless who has run away with only a slim chance of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made off' looks like 'ran away', but 'off' only tells you to scramble the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame duck is an idiom for a weak, ineffective person or one whose power has ebbed.

clue.text: Hard to get up atmosphere? That's foolish talk!

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means reading upwards, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then read upwards
the air around us

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a hard-to-generate mood, calling the whole idea nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air is an idiom for empty, boastful or pointless talk with no substance behind it.

clue.text: On target before the switch

parts.note: a butt is a target, as in the butt of a joke
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hits the mark just ahead of a change-over.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue puts 'On' first, but 'before' puts the target word ahead of it in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A button is a small switch pressed to operate a device.

clue.text: Chap goes over the line "when appropriate"

indicators.note: to go over is to turn back on oneself, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: any man's name can stand for chap; here Rob
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A man oversteps the mark, with a quoted phrase about when doing so might be fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'goes over' turns the name upside down, so it reads from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take something for one's own use, as borrowing does.

clue.text: Hurried away — was exhausted

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dashed off out of a place
second meaning: a supply came to an end

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a tired person fleeing, but 'exhausted' is about supplies being used up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both leaving at a run and a stock being used up completely.

clue.text: Story books show a certain flair

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Novels that reveal a writer's particular gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent and flair both mean a natural aptitude or gift for something.

clue.text: Undemonstrative about former family in front of journalist

parts.note: C, circa, means about
old as in previous
blood means kin or lineage
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reserved person talks about their old family while a reporter listens.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cold-blooded lacks warmth or emotion, so shows little feeling outwardly.

clue.text: Split between first to arrive

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
to reach a place is to arrive there

explanation.surface: A division among those who got there earliest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Between first' reads like a phrase about rank, but it means the first letter of 'between'.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a split or rift, for example between friends or in a wall.

clue.text: With umbrella, point at item of clothing

parts.note: umbrella as an adjective, covering everything, as in an umbrella term
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone holding a brolly gestures towards a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls are a one-piece protective garment worn over ordinary clothes, a single item though plural in form.

clue.text: Yearn for name to appear in document

indicators.note: appearing in something means being placed inside it

parts.note: a log is a written record
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Wishing to see one's name printed in an official paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To long and to yearn are both verbs for desiring something intensely.

clue.text: Embarrassed at having ran short without fruit

parts.note: red-faced with embarrassment

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: curt means brief or short
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is red-faced at running out of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense of outside, as in the hymn 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: A redcurrant is a small red berry grown on bushes, an example of fruit.

clue.text: Clothing drawer to avoid

parts.note: a drawer is something that draws
to skirt is to go round or avoid

explanation.surface: Reads like a note about a chest of drawers for clothes to be kept clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' suggests furniture, but here it is something that draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil skirt is a slim, straight-cut skirt, a garment and so an item of clothing.

clue.text: One is always right to have decoration, in general

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one word holds another

parts.note: General Custer, US cavalry commander killed at Little Bighorn
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A slogan about being right paired with a medal on a general's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the shop motto 'the customer is always right'; General Custer led the US cavalry at Little Bighorn.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'the customer is always right' makes this a cryptic description of a shopper.

clue.text: Piece to move round to the right

parts.note: to revolve is to turn round
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Reads like a board-game instruction to shift a counter round to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' suggests chess or draughts, but it is slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Piece is slang for a firearm, and a revolver is a type of handgun.

clue.text: Has finally to make an impression on race

indicators.note: finally asks for only the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the closing letter of this word
a print is an impression, as of a finger

explanation.surface: Someone at last makes their mark on a running contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint is a short, fast race run at top speed.

clue.text: Girl and chap failed to connect

parts.note: a miss is a young woman
Ed is a man's name

explanation.surface: A couple who never managed to meet up.
explanation.definitionFit: If you missed a ball or a train, you failed to make contact with it.

clue.text: What a killjoy to go off before the game!

parts.note: food that goes off is spoiling
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone who leaves just before a match begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport ruins others' fun, which is exactly what a killjoy does.

clue.text: Earnings once I'm in a new position

indicators.note: placing letters in a new position means rearranging their order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone looks forward to what they'll earn after changing jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is money received, such as wages, which is what earnings are.

clue.text: Take something in during attempt to form agreement

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to eat is to take food in

explanation.surface: Having a snack while trying to reach a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take something in' sounds like understanding, but it means swallowing food.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal pact between nations, a kind of agreement.

clue.text: Proud to be one in the lead

indicators.note: in places one item inside another

parts.note: the van, short for vanguard, is the leading position
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone takes pride in being out in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain means conceited, having too high an opinion of oneself, a sense of proud.

clue.text: Reveal girl's nearby

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, with the possessive
close means near

explanation.surface: Someone lets slip where a young woman's home is.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to make known or expose, the same as to reveal.

clue.text: Join up broken lines at last

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so its letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written for rearrangement

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the little word it follows

parts.note: the closing letter of this word

explanation.surface: A soldier finally signs up after ranks have been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' doubles as wordplay: the last letter of 'at' joins the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for the armed forces, which is what joining up means.

clue.text: Show of anger as salesman met setback?

indicators.note: a setback is a step back, so the words are read from back to front

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sales rep loses his cool after a disappointing meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A temper is an outburst of rage, as in losing one's temper.

clue.text: Appear to concentrate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: be present, show up at an event

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, 'seem to focus', but the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both turning up somewhere and giving something one's full attention.
